data.why: A yard scene where a muddy pit settles into sand, then the sand moves left to right through a furnace, a purifier tank, a crystal puller and a wafer stack, ending under a roof as a cleanroom. The camera opens close on the settling pit, follows the sand across the lawn, and goes wide when wind and rain blow mud into the open hall. Meters carry the numbers (current dropping to zero, furnace heat, billions of switches), and two newspaper sheets carry the myth and its fact.

story.title: How a Puddle of Mud Becomes a Chip Factory

ideas.idea: muddy water settles in a pit and the sand sinks to the floor
sand is silicon locked to oxygen, so no current passes through it
the sand is full of clay and iron, but a chip allows one stray atom in a billion
you pour the sand into a furnace with carbon
you heat it past 1,900 degrees and the oxygen burns off as gas
you pipe the gas into a second tank so pure silicon forms
you melt the pure silicon and pull one single crystal out of it
this machine is a Czochralski crystal puller
you slice the crystal into thin discs called wafers
machines print layer after layer of tiny switches onto each wafer with light
one chip holds over 20 billion of those switches
a single speck of dust on a wafer can kill the chip
in an open hall, wind and rain blow in mud and ruin a whole batch
you roof the hall over and push filtered air down, making a cleanroom
ordinary beach sand is not chip sand
the purest quartz comes from one small town, Spruce Pine in North Carolina
add ceiling lights and stepping stones, and the pit runs clear
calm, the finished factory stands under its roof

chain.shows: the current meter drops to zero beside the pit of sand
chain.stakes: sand cannot carry any current, so it is useless as a chip

chain.shows: dust lumps fall onto the wafer and stay on it
chain.stakes: one speck kills a chip worth far more than the dust

chain.shows: wind and rain blow mud into the open hall onto the wafers and the floor
chain.stakes: a whole batch of wafers is ruined

surprises.claim: Silicon is made by heating quartz sand with carbon in an arc furnace at roughly 1,900 to 2,000 degrees Celsius

surprises.claim: Chip-grade silicon must be about 99.9999999 percent pure, which is one foreign atom per billion
surprises.search: electronic grade silicon purity 99.9999999 percent nine nines

surprises.claim: A single modern chip can hold over 20 billion transistors
